body:
incident-bot: ALERT: kv-cache memory surge on prod-region-3 (hostpool g3d-*) — sustained allocator growth, OOM risk. paging oncall @sanjay :rotating_light:

sanjay: oncall here. seeing alerts in grafana, high GPU mem and fragmentation metrics. pulling logs now.

maya: reported spike ~ 10:06 UTC, customers A and B showing increased latency and 5xxs. looks like continuous-batching rate jumped.

cia: lia taking histograms — can you dump per-model batch sizes?

lia: grabbing quick slices. prod metrics:
- kv_cache_size_bytes: 1.9TiB (baseline ~600GiB)
- kv_arena_frag_ratio: 0.74 (normal ~0.25)
- contbatch_active_shards: 420 -> 1800 over 8m
- p99 latency: 1.2s -> 3.8s

tj: ugh. likely allocator fragmentation due to many small contiguous KV writes from larger batch sizes. i saw this with quantized models before.

sanjay: running pmap & nvidia-smi on one hot host: sharing key outputs.

opsbot: command run output:
```
$ pmap -x 12345 | tail -n 5
8024K   204K  1.2M   0.9M   0.0   anon
... (lots of small allocations) ...
```

```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv,noheader
31523 MiB
```

maya: also pulled logs — python malloc warnings and `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory` intermittently. snippet: 
```
E 10:08:12 runtime.py:512 - Torch CUDA Async: DefaultAllocator: can't allocate buffer of size 256MB
E 10:08:12 kv_cache.py:223 - insert shard failed: allocation error
```

lia: customer impact: 7 sessions aborted in last 12m, two 1-to-1 customers reported degraded interactive latency. CS notified. @csm-amy can you confirm outreach?

csm-amy: on it, pinging affected accounts and sharing temporary mitigation steps (reduce concurrency). will update if escalations.

sanjay: immediate mitigation plan (3 steps):
1) throttle continuous batching on region to reduce batch fanout (via feature flag).
2) bump slab compaction frequency on nodes (run compaction script).
3) roll back any recent batch config changes from the midnight deploy.

maya: i can flip the feature flag. small change, scope=region:prod-region-3. proposed value `contbatch_max_inflight=6` (was 48).

sanjay: do it, but set a staged rollout (all nodes in region) and monitor.

maya: executing now.
```
# flip flag via config service
curl -X POST "https://config.internal/v1/flags/contbatch_max_inflight" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"scope":"prod-region-3","value":6}'
```

opsbot: Flag update accepted, change id cfg-2026-437. Propagating to fleet.

lia: launching slab compaction against hot hosts:
```
$ ./tools/arena_compact --hosts hostpool:g3d-prod-region-3 --mode=fast
kicking compaction jobs: 32 nodes
```

tj: also applying a quick allocator tweak to reduce fragmentation pressure: increase SLAB_COMPACT_THRESHOLD from 0.2 -> 0.6 in runtime config. doing a hot-reload on canary.

sanjay: can we hot-reload without restarts?

tj: yes, runtime supports dynamic slab tuning via admin endpoint. command: 
```
curl -X POST http://admin.host:8020/tune -d '{"slab_compact_threshold":0.6}'
```

maya: canary rollout results after 90s: memory usage dropped ~30% on canary, p99 latency back to 1.4s. propagating to rest of region.

lia: contbatch_active_shards down to 620 (from 1800) after flag flip. fragmentation ratio decreasing.

opsbot: Incident annotated: ACTIONED - contbatch throttled, slab compaction run, allocator threshold bumped.

sanjay: good. short-term mitigations applied. next: root cause triage and customer communication.

maya: creating incident ticket and note for postmortem. assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml for triage.

lia: quick root-cause hypothesis: a midnight model rollout increased per-request prefix lengths causing larger KV writes and sustained batch fanout; combined with a previously undiscovered regression in the arena allocator growth path that prevented timely compaction.

tj: file a repro job in staging with the new model and high prefix distribution, instrument per-allocation sizes, and run valgrind-like checks for fragmentation patterns. also check recent allocator changes in last 2 releases.

csm-amy: CS update: sent template notice to affected customers with ETA for reduced risk; offering guided mitigations and SLO credits if they request.

maya: wrapping up for now. monitoring for 30m. please escalate if any regressions.

sanjay: thanks team. follow-ups:
- eng-runtime: postmortem + allocator patch (owner: tj)
- eng-ml: evaluate model rollout & batching behavior (owner: lia)
- support: customer outreach log (owner: csm-amy)

incident-bot: INCIDENT: 1769998888 created, severity: high, jira: REDWOOD-INC-2026.

maya: closing pager for now, leaving thread open for follow-up notes. :white_check_mark:
